channel.title: NPR Topics: Education
channel.description: We've been to school. We know how education works. Right? In fact, many aspects of learning — in homes, at schools, at work and elsewhere — are evolving rapidly, along with our understanding of learning. Join us as we explore how learning happens.

item.title: Adults have struggled to set rules for AI in school. These teens figured it out
item.description: Should students be allowed to use AI on assignments? What about on tests? Who should teach AI literacy? About 100 teenagers got together to try to decide.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Rural California school district creates space where kids can learn to swim
item.description: Not everyone has access to a public pool. But a rural school district in California just pulled together funding for a new aquatic center so kids can learn to swim.
item.content:encoded: Not everyone has access to a public pool. But a rural school district in California just pulled together funding for a new aquatic center so kids can learn to swim.

item.title: We hear from the class of 2026 on how post-grad life is going
item.description: Graduates in the class of 2026 are navigating an unusually choppy labor market. We talked to three fresh grads about their post-grad experience so far.

item.title: Meet the robots programmed by kids to speak their Indigenous languages
item.description: Many Native American languages are endangered. With the help of his mentor, a 12-year-old in Michigan hopes to help preserve his language through robotics.

item.title: No internet, no screen time? FCC weighs cutting subsidy that lowers school internet bills
